title: Remaining deferred accessibility hardening from frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize-followups's PR #375
description: PR #375 closed 4 of frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize-followups's 6 checklist items (one was already resolved on the parent task; three -- per-component maximize/resize tests, the MAXIMIZED_CHROME_ALLOWANCE_PX shorter-viewport investigation, and gating the window-resize subscription on isMaximized -- were closed in PR #375 itself) and deliberately deferred the remaining two as speculative accessibility hardening with no live reachable defect today, per that task's own decisions entries (recorded by pr-reviewer across PR #373's round-2 review and task-worker's PR #375 pass). pr-reviewer's PR #375 review independently re-confirmed the 'no live reachable defect today' claim still holds (no MetricHelp/InfoBalloon/AnchoredInfoBalloon content in any of the four chart panes has interactive elements; nothing in PR #375's diff touched that content or the maximized-overlay stacking/z-index behavior) and judged deferring further reasonable rather than rubber-stamping. Filed here (rather than left as `done: false` entries inside the now-`done` parent task file) so they stay visible/actionable per CLAUDE.md's 'every finding stays a tracked task' convention, since frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize-followups itself is now closed out.

checklist.step: Found during PR #373's round-2 re-review: `ChartFrame.tsx`'s Tab-trap scopes 'inside the dialog' purely to `frameRef`'s own DOM subtree, which doesn't account for a portaled MUI component (a `Popover`/`Menu`/`Autocomplete`) opened from content *inside* the maximized overlay -- e.g. a `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` '?' popover used throughout `PriceChart`/`OscillatorChart`/`VolumeIndicatorsChart`/`TrendStrengthChart`. Verified (real browser + a vitest/jsdom reproduction, and re-confirmed still true as of PR #375's review): opening such a popover while maximized and pressing Tab does NOT escape focus anywhere today (MUI's own `Modal`/`enforceFocus` wins the resulting tug-of-war), because every current `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` instance used inside these four chart panes renders plain `Typography` text with zero interactive elements. Would become a real keyboard-reachability bug the moment any such popover's content ever gained an interactive element (a button, a link) inside it. Worth hardening `ChartFrame`'s Tab handler to recognize when `document.activeElement` is inside some OTHER already-open modal/popover root (e.g. check for an ancestor with `role="dialog"`/`.MuiPopover-root`/`.MuiModal-root` other than its own `frameRef`) and no-op in that case, deferring entirely to that nested modal's own focus handling.

Found during PR #373's round-2 re-review: `ChartFrame.tsx`'s focus trap is per-instance only (each maximized instance's own `window`-level `keydown` listener only knows its own `frameRef`), with no coordination across multiple simultaneously-maximized instances -- unlike the sibling body-scroll-lock fix, which explicitly uses a shared module-level counter for exactly this multi-instance case. Confirmed unreachable today via an ordinary mouse click (the foreground overlay's `position: fixed; inset: 0` genuinely intercepts the pointer event at the browser's own hit-testing level) and via keyboard Tab alone (the focus trap itself prevents Tabbing to a background pane's maximize button). A related, more concerning reachability path: `ChartFrame` doesn't apply `aria-hidden`/`inert` to the rest of the page while maximized (unlike MUI's own `Modal`/`ModalManager`), so a screen-reader user in a virtual-cursor/browse-mode workflow could potentially reach a background pane's maximize button directly through the accessibility tree -- not independently confirmed against a real screen reader in any review pass so far (no AT available in this environment), so its real-world reachability remains plausible but unverified. Worth considering `aria-hidden` on `ChartFrame`'s maximized-overlay siblings and/or a shared cross-instance registry for the focus trap akin to the existing `acquireBodyScrollLock` counter, if this component is ever used somewhere multiple instances can legitimately be open at once.
